A **5–10 minute exploration**, using a prediction before each control change. The diagram and result update locally; no network service is used.

## Predict first

For COOH top, CH₃ bottom, OH left and H right, predict R/S. Will one interchange, a 180° Fischer rotation and a 90° Fischer layout rotation all have the same effect?

## Explore

1. Assign the initial configuration yourself using OH > COOH > CH₃ > H. State whether H points toward or away before interpreting the clockwise/counterclockwise trace.

2. Interchange one selected pair and reassign. Interchange a second pair and explain why two interchanges can restore the original configuration. Compare with the left/right mirror operation.

3. Reset before testing 180° and 90° page-layout rotations separately. Explain why a 90° Fischer layout operation is not equivalent to rigidly turning the actual molecule in three dimensions.

## Take-away

Write a valid rule for assigning configuration from a Fischer projection, including the lowest-priority-group correction. Why does this tool predict no optical-rotation sign?

## Model and limits

Each horizontal Fischer bond points toward the viewer and each vertical bond away. All operations rearrange the same four lactic-acid groups in that convention. A 180° in-plane Fischer rotation preserves configuration; a 90° layout rotation changes the implied configuration. R/S describes geometry, not measured (+)/(−) optical rotation.
